title: feat(types): declare `navigation` on the object-kanban and object-calendar arms, by reference to the spec (objectui#8652)
body:
Fixes #8652
Clause-②: yes

`navigation` is now declared on the `object-kanban` and `object-calendar` blocks, by reference to the spec. This is the objectui half of the maintainer ruling on objectui#8652 (verbatim 「B」): declare `navigation` on the platform element schema first, then mirror it here. The platform half shipped in `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, the release this repo resolves: `ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban']` and `ComponentPropsMap['object-calendar']` both declare `navigation: NavigationConfigSchema.optional()`.

Dispatched by the `domain:spec @ objectui` seat, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01VhxTqosz7wn54ahqyxgERT`.

## Premises, re-measured on `origin/main` `e420df31` before the first edit

- **H1, partly falsified.** On the installed 17.5.0, `navigation` is declared on `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema` and `ObjectCalendarPropsSchema`: a valid block parses, a bogus key beside it is refused with `unrecognized_keys`, and `mode: 'not-a-mode'` is refused at `navigation.mode`. ⚠️ `ObjectTimelinePropsSchema` ALSO declares it, as `NavigationConfigSchema.optional()`, with the same three verdicts. The dispatch read zero `navigation` lines in the timeline schema. The timeline is untouched here, as ordered: it belongs to objectui#8654, which remains open.
- **H2, confirmed with the TypeScript checker** (`getPropertyOfType`, not a grep). `ObjectKanbanSchema.navigation` and `ObjectCalendarSchema.navigation` were not declared, and both interfaces carry a string index signature typed `any`. Lit control: `ObjectGanttSchema.navigation` and `ObjectGridSchema.navigation` read DECLARED on the same instrument. A nonsense key reads not declared. The zod arms carried no `navigation` member either.
- **H3, partly stale.** Both renderers read the key. `ObjectKanban` reads `schema.navigation` with no cast, which compiled only through the index signature. `ObjectCalendar` read it through `(schema as any)`. `KanbanSchema` no longer declares it: that arm retired with the bare `kanban` key (objectui#8802), so `ObjectKanbanSchema` is the only kanban face.
- **H4, confirmed, and it owes more than two lines.** The parity gate booked `object-kanban.navigation` and `object-calendar.navigation` as OWED to this card. Publishing an `object`-armed input also carries the objectui#8212 obligation, a member pin apiece. See "What changed".

## What changed

- `@object-ui/types`:
  - `ObjectKanbanSchema.navigation` and `ObjectCalendarSchema.navigation` are declared on both faces: `ViewNavigationConfig` on the TS face, and `stripImportedDefaults(SpecNavigationConfigSchema).optional()` on the zod face. These are the spellings the gantt, map and gallery arms already use, taken by reference and not restated.
  - The import-boundary strip keeps the spec's `mode: 'page'` default out of a parsed document, so an absent key still reaches the renderer's own `{ mode: 'drawer' }` fallback.
- `@object-ui/plugin-calendar`: the `(schema as any).navigation` cast that objectui#8651 left for this card is gone. `OBJECT_CALENDAR_INPUTS`, shared by the `object-calendar` and `calendar` tags, publishes `navigation`.
- `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`: `OBJECT_KANBAN_INPUTS` publishes `navigation`. The read-site comment is rewritten, because it named a designer-face declaration that did not exist.
- `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`:
  - The two booked entries are struck, and the `unpublishedKeys` cap goes from 5 to 3.
  - The objectui#8176 backlog ceiling goes from 2 to 0, in all three assertions. The per-owner total for objectui#8652 goes from 2 to 0.
  - Two `MEMBER_PINS` entries are added, one per block.
  - The objectui#11168 entries are untouched. It is the last owner card, so it restores the empty ledgers.
- `calendarUnionReads-8651.test.tsx`: its one ledger entry was `navigation`, the key it deferred to this card. That entry is struck. The row that pinned the key UNDECLARED is inverted, not deleted: it now asserts the key is read AND declared.

### Pins

- `object-kanban-calendar-navigation-8652.test.ts` covers both arms against the installed spec, which it reads in the same run:
  - a valid block parses, and so does every mode;
  - a bad `mode` is refused at `navigation.mode`, and a bogus member inside the block is refused;
  - the retired `view` member is refused;
  - a CONTROL: the same bad block under an undeclared key is still accepted;
  - a parse writes no default;
  - `safeValidateSchema` agrees with the rows above;
  - on the TS face, an `Equal` assertion plus `@ts-expect-error` rows. The zod-mirror-parity ratchet cannot see a TS member that goes missing (objectui#9711), so these rows defend it.
- `kanbanNavigationMembers-8652.test.tsx` and `calendarNavigationMembers-8652.test.tsx` are the member pins. Each drives every member through a real click on the real renderer:
  - an absent key opens a drawer;
  - `none` and `preventNavigation` open nothing;
  - `new_window` and `openNewTab` open the record page in a new tab;
  - for `size` and `width`, the deprecated `width` wins, a bucket resolves through the size table, and `auto` gives the default width;
  - precedence against a parent view. The board: a parent's click handler outranks the whole key. The calendar: an overlay mode keeps the click, and any other mode hands it to the parent.

## Verification, all on `0c50a196c` (the head of this PR)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` plus the four pin files and `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`: `Test Files 303 passed (303)`, `Tests 7760 passed (7760)`.
- The dependency closures were built first (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-kanban^...' --filter '@object-ui/plugin-calendar^...' run build`). The rebuilt `dist/objectql.d.ts` carries one `navigation` member inside each of the two interface blocks. `type-check` for `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` and `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` then ran, with each script name echoed: all `Done`. `--listFilesOnly` confirms that each `tsconfig.test.json` includes the new pin files.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/ packages/plugin-calendar/`: `Test Files 123 passed (123)`, `Tests 838 passed | 95 skipped`. None of the skips is in a file this change adds or edits.
- The console closure was built, and `@object-ui/console` `type-check` is green. The neighbouring suites that read these two blocks passed: 49 files, 734 tests. They cover console `public-contract` and `public-block-binding-reach`, the app-shell block-config previews and `PageBlockInspector.retiredBlockProps`, `sdui-parser`, the `core` registry, and the prompt-keys and handler-key-read-sites script tests.
- The following gates exit 0:
  - `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:prompt-keys`, `check:doc-types`, `check:installed-pin-claims`;
  - `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims` (report-only; re-read below), `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:handler-key-reads`;
  - `check:spec-symbols`, `check:test-path-roots`, the three `check:vi-mock-*`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:registry-bare-names`;
  - `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-examples`, `check:readme-exports`, `check:sdui-registration-pins` and `check:eager-closure`, each run once its build prerequisite was met;
  - `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `type-check:coverage`, `lint:coverage`, and changeset presence, no-major, fixed and overwrite.
- Lint, as a declared narrowing. `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 11 changed TS files reports 11 files and 0 errors. The root config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` / `projectService`), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads another file. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

### Ablations, each committed first and restored to `HEAD` through `ablation-replace.mjs`

Each ablation was proven landed by anchor count and blob change. Each restore was proven by blob equals `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`, and the tree was clean afterwards.

- **TS member removed** from `ObjectKanbanSchema`: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exits 2, with TS2344 on the `Equal` assertion and TS2578 (unused `@ts-expect-error`) on the bad-mode row. The first attempt was a no-op: the tool refused it because the replacement was a prefix of the anchor. It was re-anchored and re-run.
- **Zod member removed** from the kanban arm: 5 failed and 15 passed. The five are the shape, bad `mode`, bogus member, retired `view` and `safeValidateSchema` rows.
- **Renderer read ignores the authored key** (kanban): 8 failed and 4 passed. The absent-key control, the no-flag drawer control, `size: 'auto'` and the parent-handler row stay green, as predicted.
- **Renderer read ignores the authored key** (calendar): 9 failed and 4 passed, the same shape.

## Acceptance notes

- ⚠️ **`page` opens nothing on a standalone board or calendar.** A block without `mode` resolves to `page`, the spec's default. Neither renderer hands `useNavigationOverlay` an `onNavigate`, so `page` has no channel unless a parent view supplies `onRowClick`. This is measured by mounting the real components, and it is reported as a finding. It is NOT changed here. The published input descriptions state it, and two rows per member pin hold the description to it. A renderer that learns to navigate on `page` reddens those rows, which is the signal to rewrite the description.
- `openNewTab: true` outranks an overlay `mode` as well as `page`: `{ mode: 'drawer', openNewTab: true }` opens a tab and no drawer. The spec describes the flag as "applies to page mode". This is shared hook behaviour, the grid's included. It is observed here and not pinned. Carrier: none.
- `ObjectTree.tsx` has a comment saying `navigation` is declared on one `ComponentPropsMap` entry only (`object-grid`), and that `object-tree` has no entry. That is stale since 17.5.0, which gives `object-tree` an entry declaring `navigation: z.unknown().optional()`. The tree is outside this claim. Carrier: none.
- ~~AGENTS.md #2 (docs-driven): the docs and READMEs do not document `navigation`.~~ **Superseded by round 2 (`161a5c5b4`).** The seat adopted the at-tier record's ③-3 escalation, and the docs now carry the key (see the round-2 section below). The registry descriptions carry the authoring guidance.
- `.changeset/7322-object-kanban-component-props.md` gets an append-only dated note, because its 「`navigation` is declared on neither face」 goes false here. Its frontmatter is byte-identical. `check-changeset-overwrite` reports the modification, which is its legitimate-correction case. `check:changeset-claims` named 41 pending changesets that reference touched files. Of those, only 5903 and 7917 mention `navigation`, and neither makes a claim this change falsifies.
- Overlap: objectui#10859 batch 4 holds the `ObjectFormSchema` region of the same two `@object-ui/types` files. The regions are disjoint, so whichever PR lands second merges `main`.

## Patch round 2 (written by the seat)

- Round 2 (`161a5c5b4`, AGENTS.md #2): `navigation` is documented on both blocks in `packages/plugin-kanban/README.md`, `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md`, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx`, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` and the `ObjectKanbanSchema` table of `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`. Each states the spec's `NavigationConfig` by reference (`ViewNavigationConfig`), the mode list, the absent-key drawer and the parent-view precedence, plus one sentence on the `page` caveat pointing at objectui#11293. The schema-reference sentence that called `cardTitle` and `navigation` undeclared on this face is corrected (`cardTitle` since objectui#9606). The doc gates exit 0 on `161a5c5b4`: doc-version-claims, doc-types, doc-fences, doc-example-ids, doc-example-readers, readme-exports, doc-snippets, doc-examples, new-line-citations and control-bytes.
